acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: The Hammash family’s group chat unfolds over texts, starting before the war.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: When Yousef Hammash left Gaza a year ago, his sisters decided to stay behind. We hear about the toll that separation has taken on Yousef and the sister he’s closest to, Aseel.
acts.credits: By Chana Joffe-Walt; Produced by Nancy Updike
acts.title: I’m Fine, Don’t Worry

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
Mohammed Mhawish, a reporter who left Gaza a year ago with his family, talks to a young woman in Gaza about how she manages her hunger. Israel blockaded all food from Gaza for more than two months.
Mohammed Mhawish is a contributing writer for The Nation, which is where we first read about his experiences with hunger in " What It Feels Like to Starve."
acts.credits: By Mohammed Mhawish; Produced by Diane Wu
acts.title: Week Eleven

acts.label: Coda
acts.desc: Chana gives a short update about Banias, a 9-year-old girl in Gaza she's been speaking with for months.
acts.title: Banias
